text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool eu-prod-gpu-1 queue depth > 95% for 3m, average request latency spiking. autoscaler attempted scale but hit pool max. Pager: oncall (maria).

maria: ack. I'm investigating. any obvious deploys or config changes in last 30m?

alex: looked at the runtime logs — saw massive prefix-cache-miss spikes starting ~2048129800. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 14%.

sam: autoscaler logs show scale decisions triggered but then ignored due to pool cap: 
```
2024-11-02T15:10:03Z autoscaler: decision scale_up(+6) -> rejected: pool_max_reached (configured_max=24)
2024-11-02T15:12:19Z autoscaler: scale_up(+4) -> partial_apply: only +0 available
```

kyle: I can raise the cap if we want to emergency-increase the pool. current reserved budget allows +4 GPUs in eu region.

maria: before we bump cap, let's confirm root cause. alex, what caused cache miss storm? any recent PRs?

alex: searching — there was a change merged 40m ago in runtime-config that adjusted continuous batching heuristics and prefix cache TTL via PR #4207 (commit c1a9f3b). It reduced default prefix_cache_ttl from 60s -> 5s and changed batch_aggregation_delay to 8ms -> 2ms.

liaison: support is already seeing customer errors. small set of production customers getting 5xx and throttles. I have a list: cust-redwood-42, cust-fin-112, cust-saas-7. They're reporting timeouts ~30s and intermittent 429.

maria: that PR would explain higher miss-rate (short TTL) and lower batching (smaller windows) -> reduced overall throughput -> queue growth -> autoscaler sees CPU per-pod low (because pods are CPU-bound-waiting?) and can't decide to scale effectively. we saw continuous batching flip to micro-batches.

sam: confirming metric correlation: request_per_sec per GPU dropped by 38% after PR merge, while queue_depth rose x3. Autoscaler only uses pod CPU util and pod_count to decide; with micro-batching CPU didn't show sustained spike, so scale decision mis-targeted.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) emergency revert of PR #4207 2) temporary manually increase pool cap +4 to buy time 3) patch autoscaler to read queue_depth metric for scale decisions 4) notify customers. Who can do revert?

kyle: I can bump pool cap now: `redwoodctl pools update eu-prod-gpu-1 --max-instances 28 --reason "incident 2048129999 emergency"` then request +4 in the queue. Doing it in 30s.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline: rollout request created by kyle for pool cap change (ci-job #7890).

alex: I'll open an emergency rollback PR to revert c1a9f3b and pin batch and TTL to previous values, testing locally now. Patch: 
```
- prefix_cache_ttl: 5s
- batch_aggregation_delay_ms: 2
+ prefix_cache_ttl: 60s
+ batch_aggregation_delay_ms: 8
```
PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime-config/pull/4210. aiming for hotfix deploy in 10m.

maria: liaise with support and PM about customer impact. liaision, please prepare a short blurb for affected customers and support playbook for transient 5xx/429. We need start/end window + affected endpoints.

liaison: on it. Draft message: "We're investigating increased latency/5xx on text-generation endpoints in eu. Root cause: recent batching/cache tuning. We're rolling back to previous settings; expect recovery within 15-30 minutes. We'll follow up with postmortem"

sam: I'm keeping an eye on autoscaler behavior. If we still see mismatches after rollback, we'll flip autoscaler to use queue_depth metric: `kubectl apply -f autoscaler/queue-aware.yaml` — I have that ready as a canary.

maria: update: kyle increased pool cap, autoscaler accepted manual scale; new instances provisioning. queue depth starting to drop from 2400 -> 1800.

ops-bot: CI: runtime-config hotfix PR 4210 passed tests and promoted to canary. deploy in 2m.

alex: hotfix deployed to canary, I'm watching prefix-cache-hit rate. canary pod shows hit rate back to ~88% after revert.

maria: good. rolling to prod now. alex, coordinate slow rollout. keep batching params conservative.

alex: rolling prod rollback now: applying canary settings across pool with 3-minute stagger. logs: 
```
2024-11-02T15:22:11Z runtime: prefix_cache_hit_rate=89.1%
2024-11-02T15:24:45Z runtime: avg_latency=210ms (was 1.6s)
```

liaison: support update sent to affected customers. got an initial thumbs up from cust-fin-112 saying errors reduced.

sam: autoscaler still not ideal, but queue depth now within acceptable bounds. I'll keep the queue-aware autoscaler patch in staging; need longer test before flip.

maria: we're green on immediate symptoms. Customer-facing window: 15:10 -> 15:36 UTC. Impact: elevated latency, some 5xx/429 for a subset of customers. Root cause: regression in continuous batching + prefix cache TTL change (PR c1a9f3b).

product-sre: logging this as Sev2 for postmortem. please include timeline, config diff, metric charts (queue, cache-hit, p99 latency), and decision rationale. assign to alex + sam.

maria: handing off to night oncall (sam). Summary: rollback deployed, pool cap temporarily increased then will revert to normal in 2h, autoscaler patch queued for review, customer comms sent. If recurrence, escalate to infra leads.

sam: taking over. I'll monitor for 2 hours and prepare follow-up actions: 1) revert pool max to original once stable 2) add queue_depth metric to autoscaler decisions 3) add unit/integration tests for batching heuristics 4) postmortem.

maria: thanks all. closing incident channel after 1h verification. :white_check_mark:
